thread:
Cheng: Heads-up — customer X hit unexpected double billing on a single streaming session after a reconnect + toolcall. Looks like prefetch + heartbeat interactions created two ledger entries. :frowning:
Ashwin: Ugh. any logs/trace ids? which path did the router take on reconnect?
Cheng: Repro steps in prod: open stream -> server prefetches KV -> client issues toolcall mid-stream -> client loses connection -> reconnect within 6s -> router replays from prefix -> we see two toolcall charge records. I attached console trace id: trace/78f3a
Sara: Can you paste the raw router headers from the reconnect? curious about sessiontoken vs sessionid.
Cheng: snippet of headers we saw:
```
:authority: api.redwood.prod
x-session-id: s-1234
x-session-token: t-foo-abc
x-retry-window: 6
x-prefetch: true
x-toolcall-id: tool-9a7
```
Ashwin: That x-toolcall-id should have dedupe semantics but looks like the router treated the reconnect as a fresh stream and reissued a toolcall credit.
Ken: Does the ledger dedupe key include the session-token or only the toolcall id? If only session-token changed on reconnect we might miss dedupe.
Maria: billing-bot shows two provisional credits with different path_ids: path-a and path-b. Both map to same root request.
billing-bot: Billing ledger created provisional charge 0.12 tokens (path-a) at 2358001225; provisional charge 0.12 tokens (path-b) at 2358001231. both pending.
Cheng: We think prefetch heartbeat causes an interim ledger checkpoint that pins a path id. Then reconnect generates a new path id and re-applies the toolcall charge (toolcall code executes again because router does not detect idempotent replay).
Sara: So root cause: router's reconnect path produces a new path_id and we don't attach a global idempotency key spanning reconnects.
Ashwin: Short-term mitigation: make router attach 'x-global-request-id' derived from original session-id on reconnect when within grace window. Then ledger dedupe can use that + toolcall-id.
Ken: That feels safe. Edge-case: sessions that legitimately resume after long gaps and should be billed twice. We'll restrict to reconnect < TTL (e.g., 10s).
Cheng: Also want console UX: show provisional charges grouped by global-request-id so support can see duplicates easily.
Maria: Agree. Right now console groups by path_id which splits duplicates.
Ashwin: Implementation idea: change router reconnect flow:
1) if reconnect && elapsed < reconnect_grace_window:
   - reassign path_id = original.path_id
   - preserve x-prefetch-state
   - copy x-global-request-id header
2) emit a debug metric: streaming.reconnect.reused_path=1

Add a ledger rule: dedupe key = [global_request_id, toolcall_id, op_type, truncated_prefix_hash]
Ken: We'll need to ensure this doesn't interact badly with function/tool idempotency semantics.
Sara: For toolcalls that have side-effects we still need server-side idempotency beyond billing dedupe. This is only billing dedupe.
Cheng: Also found a small truncation window problem: when client truncated prompt on reconnect, prefix-hash changed slightly (off-by-one) and dedupe missed. Need to use a fuzzy prefix-hash that's tolerant to suffix truncation.
Ashwin: Good catch. Use rolling prefix fingerprint that ignores trailing token deltas when computing dedupe key.
Maria: Can ops flag a canary for this change? We want to see provisional credits drop on 10% of traffic first.
ops-bot: Canary request accepted. Please submit PR with feature-flag gate 'reconnect-billing-dedupe' and target router group rtr-canary-10.
Ken: For telemetry: add a new gauge streaming.dedupe.miss_reason with values: missing_global_id, prefix_mismatch, time_window_expired.
Cheng: I'll open two PRs: one in router (attach global id and reuse path) and one in ledger (dedupe rule + fuzzy prefix comparator). Will include tests and console grouping change.
Sara: Tests to add: reconnect within window with identical toolcall -> single provisional. reconnect within window with truncated suffix -> single provisional (fuzzy). reconnect after window -> double provisional.
Ashwin: Also add a debug endpoint to force-expire path ids to help reproduce.
Maria: Timeline? Could we get a rollback plan in case we over-dedupe?
Cheng: Rollback is simple: flip feature flag off. We'll also add a safety throttle: if dedupe suppresses >50% of expected toolcall charges in a minute for a project, auto-disable feature for that project.
Ken: Let's document the UX in the console changelog and add a short KB for support to explain grouping and provisional vs finalized charges.
Cheng: Thanks all. I'll post PR links once ready. :thumbsup:
Ashwin: Nice. Please tag me for review on the ledger change.
Maria: Once deployed to canary, let's watch streaming.dedupe.* and billing-bot alerts.
billing-bot: Alert configured: monitor streaming.dedupe.miss_reason != missing_global_id for canary group.
Cheng: Filing the follow-up ticket to track customer refund if they were double-charged: TICKET-4521.
